references.text: The law regarding compensation for damage to livestock is also found in Exodus, where full restitution is required when someone causes the death of an animal.
Parallel verses in the same chapter reiterate the principle that whoever strikes down a beast must make restitution, life for life.
The fundamental principle of the death penalty for anyone who kills a human being is established here in Exodus.
Previous verses in the same chapter establish the death penalty for anyone who takes a human life.
Numbers emphasizes that no ransom shall be taken for the life of a murderer, but he must die—the same principle found in Leviticus.
The basic principle that human blood demands retribution because humans are created in God's image is already established in Genesis.
